claims.statement: In March 1895 Tom Allen was 54 years old, although he later gives his age as 56 in the same article.
claims.excerpt: is in excellent health at the age of 54 years

claims.statement: Tom Allen was described as the retired champion heavyweight pugilist of the world.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen, retired champion heavyweight pugilist of the world, is in excellent health at the age of 54 years.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought 23 battles between 1860 and 1879.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen was a very busy man from 1860 to 1879. In that time he fought 23 battles.

claims.statement: Tom Allen had a brother named Harry, whom Bob Smith had 'done' twice in England.
claims.excerpt: because he had done my brother, Harry, twice

claims.statement: Tom Allen came to America in 1869, after his last English fight, which was against Joe Goss.
claims.excerpt: the last fight he had in England before coming to this country in 1869

claims.statement: After the Goss fight Tom Allen got away through Canada and reached a steamer for England.
claims.excerpt: Allen got away and by going through Canada succeeded in reaching a steamer for England

claims.statement: Tom Allen's saloon, Champion's Rest, is on Market street near Seventh in St. Louis.
claims.excerpt: "Champion's Rest" is a saloon on Market street, near Seventh.
places: Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen lives upstairs over his Champion's Rest saloon.
claims.excerpt: The retired champion lives upstairs, where he keeps many trophies of victory in every part of the world.
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

claims.statement: The English championship cup Tom Allen won from Charles Davis in 1878 is kept behind the bar of his saloon in a glass case.
claims.excerpt: Back of the bar in the saloon, in a great glass case, is the English championship cup, won in a fight with Prof. Davis in 1878.
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen received a solid silver cup for winning the championship of England, inscribed May 22, 1878.
claims.excerpt: The cup that Allen got on this occasion is a massive affair of solid silver.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was shot through the back of his right hand during his fight with Charley Gallagher at Chouteau Island in August 1869.
claims.excerpt: a deep scar of a bullet wound that he got while in the midst of a fight with Charley Gallagher at Chouteau Island, up the Mississippi, in August, 1869.

claims.statement: Tom Allen broke his arm in his fight with Jem Mace at New Orleans in May 1870.
claims.excerpt: It was in this fight that Allen broke his arm and lost in the tenth round, after 50 minutes of fighting.

claims.statement: After the McCool draw, Tom Allen said he would meet Charley Gallagher in 10 minutes; the meeting was fixed for August 17, 1869.
claims.excerpt: Allen, in his anger, said that he would meet Gallagher in 10 minutes.

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he knew who fired the shot at Chouteau Island and that it was meant for him.
claims.excerpt: Allen says that he knows who fired the shot, and that it was intended for him.

claims.statement: Fred Watkins, backing Tom Allen at the Goss fight, handed a $1,000 bill to referee Eph Holland, who had made himself stakeholder.
claims.excerpt: Fred Watkins, who was backing Allen, got out a clean $1,000 bill and handed it to Holland, who had appointed himself stakeholder.

claims.statement: Tom Allen received half of the $12,000 boat money from his second fight with Mike McCool.
claims.excerpt: On my second fight with Mike McCool the boat money was $12,000, half of which came to me.

claims.statement: In 1876 Tom Allen had about $25,000 but lost most of it making a book in England.
claims.excerpt: He was about $25,000 to the good at that time, as a result of his many successes, and, with the money, he made a book through England and lost most of it.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat White in England on April 20, 1860.
claims.excerpt: Beat White, April 20, 1860. £5 a side. Forty minutes. Ten rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Nobby Hall to a draw in England on September 17, 1860.
claims.excerpt: Fought a draw with Nobby Hall, September 17, 1860. £5 a side. Forty minutes. Fifteen rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Morris Connor in England on March 20, 1861.
claims.excerpt: Beat Morris Connor, March 20, 1861. £10 a side. One hour and 10 minutes. Sixteen rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Jack Gould in England on June 8, 1861.
claims.excerpt: Beat Jack Gould, June 8, 1861. £15 a side. Fifty minutes. Eleven rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was beaten by Posh Price in England on July 28, 1862.
claims.excerpt: Beaten by Posh Price, July 28, 1862. £10 a side. Fifty minutes. Thirty-five rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bingy Rose in England on January 28, 1864.
claims.excerpt: Beat Bingy Rose, January 28, 1864. £25 a side. Twenty minutes. Ten rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was beaten by Bob Smith in England on June 2, 1864.
claims.excerpt: Beaten by Bob Smith, June 2, 1864. £5 a side. Two hours and 59 minutes. Fifty rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Jack Parkinson in England on June 13, 1865.
claims.excerpt: Beat Jack Parkinson, June 13, 1865. £25 a side. Twenty-three minutes. Eleven rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Posh Price in England on November 28, 1865.
claims.excerpt: Beat Posh Price, November 28, 1865. £25 a side. Two hours and five minutes. Forty-one rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat George Iles in England on June 13, 1866.
claims.excerpt: Beat George Iles, June 13, 1866. £25 a side. One hour and two minutes. Seventeen rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss to a draw in England on March 5, 1867, for the middle-weight championship.
claims.excerpt: Fought Joe Goss, March 5, 1867. £100 a side. Championship of middle-weights. One hour and 52 minutes. Thirty-four rounds. A draw.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Tompkin Gilbert in England on November 18, 1877.
claims.excerpt: Beat Tompkin Gilbert, November 18, 1877. £100 a side. Sixteen minutes. Five rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Charles Davis for the championship of England on April 17, 1878.
claims.excerpt: Beat Charlie Davis for the championship of England, April 17, 1878. £100 a side. Seventeen minutes. Five rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Jim Stewart in England on March 10, 1879.
claims.excerpt: Beat Jim Stewart, March 10, 1879. £50 a side. Fifty-five minutes. Sixteen rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in America on January 12, 1869.
claims.excerpt: Beat Bill Davis, January 12, 1869. $1,000 a side. Forty minutes. Forty-three rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was beaten by Charley Gallagher in two rounds on February 23, 1869.
claims.excerpt: Beaten by Charlie Gallagher, February 23, 1869. $1,000 a side. Three minutes. Two rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mike McCool to a draw on June 15, 1869, for $1,000 a side and the championship of America; the McCool party broke into the ring.
claims.excerpt: Draw with Mike McCool, June 15, 1869. $1,000 a side and the championship of America. Twelve minutes. Nine rounds. McCool party broke in the ring.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Charley Gallagher in eleven rounds on August 17, 1869, at Chouteau Island.
claims.excerpt: Beat Charlie Gallagher, August 17, 1869. $1,000 a side. Twenty-one minutes. Eleven rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was beaten by Jem Mace in ten rounds on May 10, 1870, at New Orleans, for $5,000 and the championship of the world.
claims.excerpt: Beaten by Jem Mace, May 10, 1870. $5,000 and the championship of the world. Fifty minutes. Ten rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen was matched with Mike McCool for $2,500 a side and the championship on June 2, 1870; McCool forfeited $1,000 and the match was off.
claims.excerpt: Matched with Mike McCool, June 2, 1870. $2,500 a side and the championship. McCool forfeited $1,000.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Jim Gallagher in fourteen rounds on November 7, 1870.
claims.excerpt: Beat Jim Gallagher, November 7, 1870. Allen staking $1,000 to $500. Twenty-one minutes. Fourteen rounds.
places: sandbar at the foot of Chouteau avenue

claims.statement: In 1870, while working and sparring in New York on exhibition with Jem Mace, Tom Allen learned that McCool had forfeited.
claims.excerpt: while he was in New York working and sparring, on exhibition with Mace, he got word that McCool had forfeited.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Mike McCool in seven rounds on September 23, 1873, for $2,000 a side and the championship.
claims.excerpt: Beat Mike McCool, September 23, 1873. $2,000 a side and the championship. Nineteen minutes. Seven rounds.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Ben Hogan in three rounds on November 18, 1873.
claims.excerpt: Beat Ben Hogan, November 18, 1873. Seven minutes. Three rounds. The ring broken into by Hogan's friends and pistols pointed at Allen's head.

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Joe Goss in Kentucky on September 7, 1876, for $2,500 a side; the referee gave the fight to Goss on an alleged foul.
claims.excerpt: Beat Joe Goss, September 7, 1876. $2,500 a side. Swindled out of the money by alleged foul. One hour and fifty minutes. Thirty-seven rounds.

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: When we fought in the open, the air was always changing. A man would get a good breath when he was resting, instead of having to breathe the foul stuff that they get to-day.
quotes.topic: on indoor arenas versus open-air fights

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: They ought to be allowed to rest while they have a bit of a chance. In the old days prize fighters were in better health all alone than they are in these times.
quotes.topic: on crowds around fighters between rounds

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: I'm of the notion that the best man of 'em all now is Corbett. I won't attempt to compare him with any of the best men of 25 and 30 years ago, for methods are altogether different.
quotes.topic: on Corbett as the best fighter now

fights.excerpt: Beat White, April 20, 1860. £5 a side. Forty minutes. Ten rounds.
Fought a draw with Nobby Hall, September 17, 1860. £5 a side. Forty minutes. Fifteen rounds.
Beat Morris Connor, March 20, 1861. £10 a side. One hour and 10 minutes. Sixteen rounds.
Beat Jack Gould, June 8, 1861. £15 a side. Fifty minutes. Eleven rounds.
Beaten by Posh Price, July 28, 1862. £10 a side. Fifty minutes. Thirty-five rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's own account says he went at Price again three years later and won.

fights.excerpt: Beat Bingy Rose, January 28, 1864. £25 a side. Twenty minutes. Ten rounds.
Beaten by Bob Smith, June 2, 1864. £5 a side. Two hours and 59 minutes. Fifty rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's own account in the article says Smith beat him in fifty minutes, and that the fight was barefoot in the open country. The record gives 2 hours 59 minutes.

fights.excerpt: Beat Jack Parkinson, June 13, 1865. £25 a side. Twenty-three minutes. Eleven rounds.
Beat Posh Price, November 28, 1865. £25 a side. Two hours and five minutes. Forty-one rounds.
fights.notes: Rematch with Price; Allen's account gives 41 rounds at 146 pounds.

fights.excerpt: Beat George Iles, June 13, 1866. £25 a side. One hour and two minutes. Seventeen rounds.
Fought Joe Goss, March 5, 1867. £100 a side. Championship of middle-weights. One hour and 52 minutes. Thirty-four rounds. A draw.
Beat Tompkin Gilbert, November 18, 1877. £100 a side. Sixteen minutes. Five rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's account says Gilbert had the English championship and that Allen won it from him in sixteen minutes.

fights.excerpt: Beat Charlie Davis for the championship of England, April 17, 1878. £100 a side. Seventeen minutes. Five rounds.
fights.notes: Text says $500 a side and a gentleman's cup, and calls him Professor Charles Davis; the record says £100 a side.

fights.excerpt: Beat Jim Stewart, March 10, 1879. £50 a side. Fifty-five minutes. Sixteen rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's own account: Stewart ran around the ropes and Allen finished him with a deadener.

fights.excerpt: Beat Bill Davis, January 12, 1869. $1,000 a side. Forty minutes. Forty-three rounds.
Beaten by Charlie Gallagher, February 23, 1869. $1,000 a side. Three minutes. Two rounds.
fights.notes: The prose says February 22, 1869. Allen slipped in a snow-filled hole in the ring in the second round and was hit on the neck. The record table's three minutes is kept; the text gives no duration.

fights.stakes: $1,000 a side and the championship of America
fights.excerpt: Draw with Mike McCool, June 15, 1869. $1,000 a side and the championship of America. Twelve minutes. Nine rounds. McCool party broke in the ring.
fights.notes: The prose says the draw came at the end of the tenth round; the record says nine. The McCool party broke into the ring.

fights.excerpt: Beat Charlie Gallagher, August 17, 1869. $1,000 a side. Twenty-one minutes. Eleven rounds.
fights.notes: A shot fired from ringside hit Allen's right hand; the lead was pushed out and the fight resumed after seven minutes. Allen said the shot was meant for him.

fights.stakes: $5,000 and the championship of the world
fights.excerpt: Beaten by Jem Mace, May 10, 1870. $5,000 and the championship of the world. Fifty minutes. Ten rounds.
fights.notes: Allen broke his arm in this fight.

fights.excerpt: Matched with Mike McCool, June 2, 1870. $2,500 a side and the championship. McCool forfeited $1,000.
fights.notes: McCool forfeited $1,000, and the match was off. The text says Allen learned of the forfeit while in New York.

fights.place: Sandbar at the foot of Chouteau avenue
fights.excerpt: Beat Jim Gallagher, November 7, 1870. Allen staking $1,000 to $500. Twenty-one minutes. Fourteen rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's account: Gallagher, a Western fighter, had been talking, and Allen put up $1,000 against Gallagher's $500.

fights.excerpt: Beat Mike McCool, September 23, 1873. $2,000 a side and the championship. Nineteen minutes. Seven rounds.
fights.notes: Allen's second fight with McCool, when the boat money was $12,000.

fights.excerpt: Beat Ben Hogan, November 18, 1873. Seven minutes. Three rounds. The ring broken into by Hogan's friends and pistols pointed at Allen's head.
fights.notes: Allen's account: Hogan's friends rushed into the ring with pistols and pointed them at him; Allen was not hurt.

fights.excerpt: Beat Joe Goss, September 7, 1876. $2,500 a side. Swindled out of the money by alleged foul. One hour and fifty minutes. Thirty-seven rounds.
fights.notes: Disputed. The record table says Allen beat Goss, but the text says referee Eph Holland gave the fight to Goss on an alleged foul and kept Fred Watkins's $1,000 stake. Goss was jailed for a year and a half; Allen fled to England.

notes: Age conflicts: 54 at the start, 56 later. The record table and the prose conflict on several dates and details (Gallagher Feb 22/23, McCool draw rounds, Goss result, Charles Davis stakes); see fight notes. Allen's own list covers 23 fights plus one forfeited match, as the article says.
